sections.lead: The Musée de la civilisation wanted an engaging, fluid experience that encourages people to *discover its collections, play with them and contribute to them*. sections.label: The context
prose: The Musée de la civilisation is a place of inquiry, study and documentation that seeks to understand and interpret the world. Its research activities make the institution a national reference.

Its collections are kept in two different storage facilities. For this project, more than 9,600 objects and 45,000 archive documents and books were to be digitized and presented online for the public to consult, inspect and virtually play with. How the objects would be presented, and how people would interact with them, was not clearly defined yet.

sections.label: The approach
prose: Every app or website should start with the target audience in mind.

With the museum team, we developed two main user profiles with different backgrounds and needs: *Nicole, an amateur researcher*, and *Jérôme, a member of the general public*. Together, we then created a sequential user story map for each one, aimed at deepening their relationship with the museum along the way.
This let the museum team clearly see what mattered most, and what could come in later development phases without losing people’s interest.

items.p: They use cookies to remember the last chunks of information displayed, to tailor the experience to the needs and context of most users.
